title: A cheap, exact "store changed since the newest copy" signal a host can read before pushing
outcome: A cheap, exact "store changed since the newest copy" signal a host can read before pushing
acceptance: A host can tell, without a full capture, whether the store changed since the newest copy. The signal is exact for everything a copy restores: every table a restore brings back, including claims, control rows and delivery state, not only the work cut. It is reported in `backup status --json`, in the receipt table and its test, or used by `backup push` to skip a capture. A test shows a change in each kind of restored row flips it. If an exact store-wide marker cannot be made cheap, the design record says so, and nothing approximate ships described as exact.

Skipping a capture never on its own refreshes qualification: `local_backed_up` still requires a verified copy within the window. Whether an unchanged marker may extend an existing copy's observed-equal time is decided in a design review with Engram::Fable and a read-only Codex explorer before any code, and recorded on this item.
docs/host-checklist.md tells the host how to use the signal with the push cadence, and the change is sent to TermAl's coordinator, with the mailbox sequence and TermAl's answer recorded here.

completion.summary: Delivered exact settled-byte same-build backup check/compression reuse with mandatory target confirmation, full fallback and missing-copy replacement checks; reports capture_check and honest no-cheap-marker/cost/cadence docs. Full gate, Codex/Claude pair, independent acceptance3/3 passed; committed, pushed and installed, four live stores ready, no restart.
